root_cause.text: In `sched_mm_cid_exit()`, the code incorrectly assumes that after a mode switch from per-CPU CID to per-task mode, the CID is always CPU-owned (ONCPU bit set), but the TRANSIT bit can remain set without the ONCPU bit if the task never scheduled after the TRANSIT was set by another CPU, leading `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()` to misinterpret the CID value and cause an out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that T1 exits with `MM_CID_TRANSIT` set after not having scheduled since CPU0 set it, and `sched_mm_cid_exit()` calls `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()` which clears the unset ONCPU bit and then uses the CID (including the TRANSIT bit) as a bit number, causing an out-of-bounds access. The patch adds a check `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` to validate CPU ownership before proceeding.

The patch adds a check `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` to validate CPU ownership before proceeding.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update comment in sched_mm_cid_exit to accurately describe handling of TRANSIT bit and CPU CID ownership when dropping the CID.
intent_record.what: Replaced a block comment in `sched_mm_cid_exit` that previously stated 'The CPU CID is still valid and does not have MM_CID_TRANSIT set as the mode change has just taken effect under mm::mm_cid::lock. Drop it.' with a new comment: 'already and dealt with an eventually set TRANSIT bit. If the CID is owned by the CPU then drop it.'
intent_record.how: No functional change; the updated comment better describes the existing code logic without affecting runtime behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard the clearing of ONCPU bit and dropping of CID to only when the CID is currently marked as on a CPU.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` around the existing operations that clear the ONCPU bit and drop the CID.
intent_record.how: The function now only performs the CID unset and drop logic when the CID currently has the ONCPU bit set, preventing operations on CIDs that are not in the expected state.
